name: Lenalidomide
route_note: oral capsules once daily, typically days 1–21 of 28-day cycles; dispensed under a risk-management programme

discovery.note: A 4-amino glutarimide analogue of thalidomide with greater immunomodulatory potency and less neurotoxicity and sedation.

tagline: Thalidomide analogue that degrades Ikaros proteins; backbone of myeloma therapy
summary: Lenalidomide is an oral thalidomide analogue that redirects the cereblon E3 ubiquitin ligase to degrade transcription factors essential for myeloma cells. It is a backbone of multiple myeloma treatment, including long-term maintenance after transplant, and is used in del(5q) myelodysplastic syndrome and several lymphomas.
mechanism: Lenalidomide binds cereblon (CRBN), the substrate receptor of the CRL4 E3 ubiquitin ligase, and acts as a 'molecular glue' that recruits neosubstrates — the lymphoid transcription factors Ikaros (IKZF1) and Aiolos (IKZF3) — for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation.

Loss of these factors kills myeloma cells (via IRF4 and MYC downregulation) and de-represses IL-2 in T cells, enhancing T-cell and NK-cell immunity. In del(5q) MDS, degradation of casein kinase 1α is selectively lethal to cells with only one copy of CSNK1A1.
uses: Multiple myeloma (with dexamethasone, in combinations, and as post-transplant maintenance)
Transfusion-dependent anaemia in low/intermediate-1-risk MDS with del(5q)
Mantle cell lymphoma after prior therapy
Previously treated follicular and marginal zone lymphoma (with rituximab)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved for del(5q) myelodysplastic syndrome with a restricted distribution programme.

history.title: Multiple myeloma
history.detail: Approved with dexamethasone for previously treated myeloma (MM-009/010).

history.title: Cereblon
history.detail: Ito, Handa and colleagues (Science) identify cereblon as the primary target of thalidomide.

history.title: Ikaros degradation
history.detail: Krönke et al. and Lu et al. (Science) show lenalidomide induces degradation of IKZF1 and IKZF3.

history.title: Maintenance
history.detail: FDA approves lenalidomide maintenance after autologous transplant.

history.title: BMS acquisition
history.detail: Bristol-Myers Squibb acquires Celgene for about $74 billion; Revlimid is a central asset.

history.title: Volume-limited generics
history.detail: Limited-volume US generics launch under patent settlements; unrestricted entry is permitted from 31 January 2026.

safety.boxed_warning: Boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity (REMS programme), haematological toxicity in del(5q) MDS, and venous and arterial thromboembolism.

facts: It became one of the world's best-selling drugs, with annual Revlimid sales exceeding $12 billion at its peak.
